title: English for Secretaries & Admin Assistants
overview: This practical English-language course equips secretaries, administrative assistants, receptionists, and office coordinators with the communication skills needed to support day-to-day office operations confidently and professionally. Participants develop the vocabulary, grammar, tone, and fluency required to manage correspondence, telephone calls, appointments, meetings, visitors, documents, and workplace requests. Emphasis is placed on clear, accurate, courteous English across spoken, written, and digital office interactions.
audience: Secretaries, executive secretaries, and personal assistants.
Administrative assistants, office coordinators, and administrative officers.
Receptionists, front-desk personnel, and customer-facing support staff.
Professionals seeking to improve English communication for administrative responsibilities.
methodology: Interactive language instruction combines short demonstrations, guided speaking practice, role-played telephone calls and visitor interactions, email-writing workshops, meeting simulations, listening tasks, document-editing exercises, vocabulary drills, and individualized feedback. Participants complete realistic office communication assignments and a final integrated administrative scenario.
competencies: Professional oral communication and active listening in office settings.
Accurate and courteous business email and administrative writing.
Telephone etiquette, call screening, and message taking in English.
Appointment scheduling, meeting coordination, and minute-taking language.
Office vocabulary, document handling, and information clarification.
Cross-cultural communication, confidentiality, and professional tone.
objectives: Use appropriate English vocabulary and expressions for common administrative tasks.
Greet visitors, handle inquiries, and communicate professionally in person and by phone.
Draft and revise clear emails, notices, invitations, and routine office messages.
Schedule appointments, confirm arrangements, and resolve calendar conflicts politely.
Prepare meeting agendas, capture action points, and write concise meeting minutes.
Read and interpret workplace instructions, schedules, forms, and business documents.
Ask clarifying questions, relay messages accurately, and follow up on requests.
Apply suitable grammar, tone, and etiquette in multicultural professional environments.
